items.prompt: What is it called when a seed starts to grow?

options.why: Pollination is when pollen moves from flower to flower.
Evaporation is when a liquid turns into a gas.
Reflection is when light bounces off something.

hints: This word is used when a seed wakes up and sprouts.
It is the first stage in the life of a new plant.
Look for the word that is about seeds, not light or water.
items.explanation: Germination is when a seed starts to grow. A root grows out first, then a shoot.

items.prompt: Put the stages of a bean seed growing in order.
items: The seed takes in water and swells.
A root grows down out of the seed.
A shoot grows up towards the light.
hints: Think about what a dry seed needs before anything else happens.
The part that holds the plant in the soil comes out first.
Start with the seed getting wet.
items.explanation: A seed swells with water, then a root grows down. Next a shoot grows up, and its first leaves open to catch light.

items.prompt: Choose 3 things most seeds need to germinate.

options.why: Most seeds germinate in the dark soil, using food stored inside them.
Seeds can germinate on wet cotton wool, without any soil.

hints: Think about seeds sprouting on wet cotton wool in a dark cupboard.
Seeds carry their own food to start growing.
Cross out anything a seed in a dark jar would not have.
items.explanation: Most seeds need water, warmth and air to germinate. They do not need light or soil yet, because they use food stored inside the seed.

items.prompt: Rudi puts bean seeds on wet cotton wool in a warm, dark cupboard. Will they germinate?

options.text: No, because seeds always need light to start growing.
options.why: Seeds start growing using food stored inside them. They do not need light yet.

options.text: Yes, because they have water, warmth and air.
No, because seeds need soil to germinate.
options.why: Seeds can germinate without soil if they have water, warmth and air.

options.text: Yes, but only in the daytime.
options.why: Inside a dark cupboard, day or night makes no difference.

hints: List what the seeds have in the cupboard.
Remember the three things most seeds need to germinate.
Check each need, one by one.
items.explanation: The seeds have water, warmth and air, so they will germinate. Light is not needed until the leaves must make food.

items.prompt: Rudi leaves the seedlings in the dark cupboard. Two weeks later, they are tall, thin and yellow. What do they need?

options.why: They have had darkness for two weeks. That is the problem.
Seedlings need warmth to grow well, not cold.
Water is not the problem here. Something else is missing.

hints: After germination, the seedling must make its own food.
Which part makes food, and what does it use?
Think about what is missing inside a cupboard.
items.explanation: Once the stored food runs out, seedlings make food in their leaves using light. Without light they grow pale, thin and weak.

items.prompt: The table shows two bean plants after 2 weeks. How much taller is the plant on the windowsill?

head: Place
Height after 2 weeks (cm)
figure.alt: Table: the plant on a sunny windowsill grew to 14 cm. The plant inside a fridge grew to 3 cm.

hints: Find both heights in the table.
Taller by how much means find the difference.
Start with the bigger height and take away the smaller one.
items.explanation: 14 cm take away 3 cm is 11 cm. The fridge was cold and dark, so that plant grew much less.

items.prompt: Sort these. Do they help a plant grow well, or stop it growing well?
hints: Think about what a healthy plant gets every day.
Plants need light, water, warmth and minerals.
Start with sunlight. Does a plant need it?
items.explanation: Plants grow well with light, water, warmth and minerals from the soil. Weeks of darkness, salty water and freezing weather all harm them.

items.prompt: Farmers often soak rice seeds in water for a day before sowing them. Why?

options.text: to wash the light out of the seeds
options.why: Seeds do not hold light. Soaking gives them water.
Seeds need warmth, not cold, to germinate.

options.text: to remove the food stored inside
options.why: Seeds need their food store to start growing.

options.text: to give the seeds water so they start to germinate

hints: Think about what a dry seed needs to wake up.
Remember the three things seeds need to germinate.
Which of those does soaking give?
items.explanation: Seeds need water to germinate. Soaking lets rice seeds take in water, so they start growing sooner.

items.prompt: Plants on a windowsill slowly bend towards the window. Why?

options.text: because they grow towards the light
to get away from the wall
options.why: Plants do not move away from walls.

options.text: because wind from the window pushes them
options.why: The bending happens even with the window closed.
Plants grow towards light, not towards cold.

hints: Think about what comes in through a window.
Plants need something from the window to make food.
Ask: what is brighter on the window side?
items.explanation: Plants grow towards light because they need it to make food. The stems bend so the leaves face the window.

items.prompt: Lia wants to test if seeds need warmth to germinate. Which two pots should she compare?

head: Pot
Water
Place
figure.alt: Table of four pots. A: water, warm cupboard. B: water, fridge. C: no water, warm cupboard. D: no water, fridge.

options.why: These pots differ in water, not warmth.
These pots differ in water and warmth, so the test is not fair.
Neither pot has water, so no seeds will germinate in either.

hints: Only the thing being tested should be different.
Find two pots with the same water but a different place.
Look for two pots that both have water.
items.explanation: Pots A and B both have water and are both dark. Only the temperature is different, so this is a fair test of warmth.

items.prompt: A bean seed germinates on wet cotton wool in a dark box. Its shoot grows 5 cm. Where did the food for this growth come from?

options.why: Cotton wool only holds water. It has no food for the seed.
The box was dark, so the seedling could not make food yet.
Water helps the seed swell, but water is not food.

hints: The box was dark, so leaves could not make food.
Cotton wool and water are not food.
Think about what a seed carries inside it.
items.explanation: A seed carries a store of food inside it. The seedling uses this food until its leaves can make food using light.

items.prompt: Mia measured her bean plant. On Monday it was 4 cm tall. On Friday it was 9 cm tall.
hints: Find the two heights in the story.
To find how much it grew, take the first height from the second.
items.explanation: The plant grew 9 take away 4, which is 5 cm. A table is a clear way to record measurements.

parts.prompt: How many centimetres did the plant grow?
Which is a clear way to record the heights?

items.prompt: Which part of a seed grows out first?

options.why: Leaves come later.
Flowers come much later.
Fruit comes at the end.

items.explanation: The root grows down first. It takes in water and anchors the seedling.

items.prompt: What is it called when seeds are spread away from the parent plant?

options.why: That is when a seed starts to grow.
That is moving pollen between flowers.
That is a plant drooping.

items.explanation: Seed dispersal means seeds are carried away from the parent plant.

items.prompt: Why is it good for seeds to land far from the parent plant?

options.text: They do not have to share light and water.

options.why: Noise does not help.
That is not the reason.
Plants do not grow upside down.

hints: Too many plants crowd each other.
items.explanation: Far from the parent, each plant has its own space, light and water.

items.prompt: Which seed is carried by the wind?

options.why: A coconut floats on water.
A burr sticks to fur.
Animals eat blackberries.

items.explanation: Dandelion seeds are light and fluffy. The wind carries them far away.

items.prompt: A coconut floats across the sea and lands on a beach. How was its seed spread?

options.why: It floated.
It floated on the sea.
Magnets do not move seeds.

items.explanation: Coconuts float, so the sea carries them to new beaches.

items.prompt: Birds eat berries. Later the seeds fall in their droppings. What have the birds done?

options.why: They moved seeds.
That does not happen.
Seeds can grow after.

items.explanation: Animals can carry seeds in their bodies and drop them far from the parent plant.

items.prompt: What is the best way to measure how tall a bean plant is?

options.why: Scales measure mass.
A clock measures time.
A thermometer measures heat.

hints: Centimetres are a unit of length.
items.explanation: We use a ruler to measure height in centimetres.

items.prompt: How is the seed spread? Sort the plants.
items.explanation: Dandelion and sycamore seeds blow in the wind. Coconut and water lily seeds float. Burrs stick to fur and animals eat blackberries.

items.prompt: Is it a seed? Sort the cards.
hints: A seed can grow into a plant.
Petals are part of a flower.
items.explanation: Beans, peas and sesame seeds are seeds. A carrot is a root, a leaf is a leaf and a petal is part of a flower.

items.prompt: Choose all the things a seedling needs to grow healthy.
items.explanation: A seedling needs light, water and warmth. Music and sweets do not help it.

items.prompt: Put the steps in order, from pollen to a new seed growing.
hints: Seeds must be spread before they grow.
items.explanation: Pollen reaches the flower, then seeds form. The fruit ripens and the seeds are spread. Then a seed can germinate.

items.prompt: Match each seed part to its job.
items.explanation: The coat protects the seed. The root grows down and the shoot grows up. The food store feeds the baby plant.

items.prompt: A seed starts to ___ when it has water and warmth. It grows into a ___.
hints: A baby plant is called this.
items.explanation: A seed germinates with water and warmth. It grows into a seedling.

items.prompt: The bean plant is 4 cm on Day 1 and grows 2 cm each day. Complete the table.
head: Day
Height (cm)
items.explanation: Add 2 cm each day: 4, 6, 8 and 10.

items.prompt: Lia plants 10 bean seeds in wet cotton wool. She puts 5 in a warm room and 5 in a fridge. After a week, 4 of the seeds in the warm room have germinated. None in the fridge has.

parts.prompt: Why did the fridge seeds not germinate?

hints: What was different in the fridge?
items.explanation: Four seeds germinated in the warm room. The fridge was too cold for the seeds to start growing.

items.prompt: A bean plant is 5 cm tall on Monday. It grows 2 cm each day. How tall is it on Wednesday?
hints: Monday to Tuesday is one day.
items.explanation: Tuesday is 5 + 2 = 7 cm. Wednesday is 7 + 2 = 9 cm.

items.prompt: Tap the seed.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: seed, seedling, plant and tree.

hints: It is where a plant starts.
items.explanation: A seed is the small part that can grow into a new plant.

items.prompt: Tap the seedling.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: seed, seedling, plant and tree.

items.explanation: A seedling is a young plant that has just grown from a seed.

items.prompt: When a seed starts to grow, we say it ___.
items.explanation: Germination is when a seed starts to grow into a new plant.

items.prompt: Draw and label a bean seedling. Show the root, the shoot and a leaf.

criteria.label: Draws a seedling with a root
Draws the shoot and a leaf

items.explanation: A bean seedling has a root that grows down and a shoot that grows up with leaves.

items.prompt: Four bean seeds are tested. A is dry and warm. B is wet and warm. C is wet and cold. D is dry and cold. Which germinates?

options.why: It is dry.
It is cold.
It is dry and cold.

items.explanation: Seeds need both water and warmth. Only seed B has both.

items.prompt: Maple seeds spin like tiny helicopters as they fall. Why does this help the plant?

options.why: The spin makes it fall slower.

options.text: It makes the seed grow faster.
options.why: Spinning does not change growth.

options.text: It slows the fall, so the wind carries the seed further.
It stops the seed from germinating.
options.why: It does not do that.

hints: Slow falling means more time in the air.
items.explanation: Spinning slows the seed. The wind has more time to carry it away from the parent tree.

items.prompt: A dandelion makes 200 seeds. One in ten lands on good soil and grows. How many seeds grow?
items.explanation: One tenth of 200 is 20. About 20 seeds grow.
